model.rationale: The fundamentals point to a comfortable Democratic hold: an D+11 seat, an incumbent who has raised over $850K, and prediction markets pricing her near 97%. With no polls or expert ratings suggesting otherwise, the safe-D assessment stands.
model.watch: Any late polling showing a much tighter race or unexpected outside spending against Escobar would warrant a downgrade.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Veronica Escobar seeks another term in this El Paso–area House district, which leans Democratic by about 11 points on the partisan baseline. She enters the general election as a well-established incumbent, having raised roughly $860,000, while Republican challenger Adam Bauman reports no fundraising figures and no outside spending has materialized on either side.

No public polls or expert race ratings are available, so the outlook rests on district fundamentals, incumbency, and prediction markets, which price Escobar's chances at about 97%. All signs point to a comfortable Democratic hold, with the main uncertainty being the absence of direct polling in the district.
